title: Mirror context superposition vs Parameter Superposition
hypothesis: A learned orthogonal Mirror task coordinate can retrieve multiple useful task maps from one shared physical operator with a better byte-quality-interference frontier than fixed-context PSP and simple task-code low-rank sharing.
physical_object: One shared physical linear operator and its deterministic task-map reconstruction state
mirror_coordinate: A learned task-specific 2D rotation angle with one learned shared base angle

task.teacher_family: seeded orthogonal conjugates of a common spectrum with task-specific 2D rotations

development.selection_metric: mean test MSE; rank only among predeclared candidates

storage.serializer: numpy savez compressed=False, native fitted dtype retained

compute.active_compute_proxy: dense linear multiply MACs; report method-specific transform work separately

success_gate: At least 3/4 fresh seeds: Mirror MSE <= 1.10x best control, <=75% independent bytes, and lower error than PSP and task-code at payload bytes within 10%.
failure_gate: Mirror test MSE >1.25x best control on at least 3/4 fresh seeds, or no byte-quality frontier improvement over simpler controls.
boundaries: post-fit representation screen; not optimizer learning efficiency or capacity
